videos.script: Lesson 15 built structs one field at a time. This lesson puts a struct inside another one, without giving it a name. {{embed}} That is called embedding. The inner struct's fields can then be reached as if they belonged to the outer one. An employee has a name because the person inside it has one. {{notis}} It looks like inheritance, and it is not. A function that asks for a Person refuses an Employee. The compiler says so, and you will see the message. You hand over the part, not the whole. {{clash}} Then the awkward case. Two embedded structs can bring two fields with the same name. Go refuses to guess which one you meant, and tells you where. {{json}} Except in one place. The JSON encoder drops both fields without a word, and you will watch a name disappear from the output. By the end you can build a type out of smaller ones, and say exactly which field a name reaches.
